newsitem.title: INDIA: India's INDAL meets ecology standard.
newsitem.headline: India's INDAL meets ecology standard.

text.p: The Indian Aluminium Company Ltd (INDAL) has received environment management certifications -- ISO 14001 -- for its three diverse business units, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

He said INDAL's bauxite mines in western Maharashtra state, a power plant in eastern Orissa state and an electronics plant in Karnataka in the south have been certified for best environment practices by a British certification firm.
"In the next three years all relevant plants of INDAL will be certified for environment management systems," V.K. Bhatnagar told reporters.
ISO 14001 is a global code of ecological standards set by the International Standards Organisations.
INDAL's units have been certified by U.K.-based Aspects Certification Services, company officials said.
INDAL is an associate company of Canada's Alcan Aluminium, which holds 34.6 percent of its equity.
India's largest manufacturer of finished aluminium products, it posted a net profit of 1.15 billion rupees in 1995/96 (April-March).
Bhatnagar said the bauxite mine at Durgmanwadi in Maharashtra was the world's first to be certified for environmentally benign mining technologies.
It had replaced traditional drilling and blasting with ripping and dozing to eliminate noise and dust pollution.

INDAL's 67.5 MW thermal power plant at Hirakud in Orissa is the first power plant in Asia to be certified as using technologies for resource conservation, pollution abatement and waste utilisation, he said.

Bhatnagar said the company's printed circuit board plant at Nanjangud in Karnataka used technologies that eliminated hazardous chemicals, reduced ozone-depleting substances and recycled 70 percent of the plant's water consumption.
